result.topic_en: After defining 'associated' (socia) residues whose product is congruent to 1 mod P, Euler states and begins proving the theorem that x^n - 1 can be divisible by a prime P for at most n values of x less than P, starting with the cases n = 1, 2, 3.

items.english: For the form x^n - 1 to become divisible by the prime number P, taking x < P, this cannot happen in more than n ways.
